title: Customer statement running balance computed with a triangular join
prompt: Statement generation. It is fine for normal customers (fewer than 200 payments). For partner accounts (up to 180k
Settled or Refunded payments, statements usually cover one month) it hits the 30 s command timeout. Plan: nested
loops; the inner subquery reads all of the customer's payments again for every output row. Settlement batches stamp
the same PaidAt on 50-500 payments. Accountants compare the RunningBalance column line by line with the previous
system, so the values must not change. The balance is cumulative from the customer's first payment, not from @From.
data_notes: Azure SQL Database, General Purpose Gen5, 8 vCores, compatibility level 160. READ_COMMITTED_SNAPSHOT ON. Query Store READ_WRITE. Collation SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS. All foreign keys are trusted. Statistics: auto create and auto update ON; a nightly job updates Orders, OrderLines and Payments with FULLSCAN.

Payments: 60M rows. Status: Settled 88%, Failed 6%, Refunded 4% (negative Amount), Pending 2%. ExternalRef is NULL for ~30%; non-NULL values are almost unique, with a few duplicates from provider retries. Partner accounts have up to 180k Settled or Refunded payments each. Settlement batches stamp the same PaidAt on 50-500 payments.

Orders: 30M rows, 2016 to now, ~12k per day now. The 25 partner customers own ~9M orders (30%), up to 1.2M each. Other customers average ~10 orders (max ~400). The density estimate for CustomerID is ~15 rows. Status: Shipped 83.8%, Cancelled 7%, Paid 6%, Returned 3%, Pending 0.2% (~60k rows, all from the last 72 hours). SalesChannel: Web 62%, Store 20%, Partner 12%, Phone 6%. PromoCode is NULL for 85%. ShipRegionID is NULL for Store pickups (~20%). OrderDate is datetime2(7); Partner and Store imports stamp one timestamp on a whole batch, so many orders of one customer share an OrderDate.
baseline_sql: JOIN qe.Orders o2 ON o2.OrderID = p2.OrderID
JOIN qe.Orders o ON o.OrderID = p.OrderID

correct_families.description: A window sum with RANGE semantics over all history up to @To, with the @From filter applied outside the window.
reference_sql: SUM(p.Amount) OVER (ORDER BY p.PaidAt RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS RunningBalance
JOIN qe.Orders o ON o.OrderID = p.OrderID

correct_families.description: Sum per PaidAt first, run a ROWS window over the distinct timestamps, then join the balance back to the payments.
reference_sql: SELECT p.PaidAt, SUM(SUM(p.Amount)) OVER (ORDER BY p.PaidAt ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS RunningBalance
JOIN qe.Orders o ON o.OrderID = p.OrderID
JOIN qe.Orders o ON o.OrderID = p.OrderID

traps.why: The original uses <=, so every payment of one settlement batch shows the same balance. A ROWS frame gives each tied row a different partial balance.
traps.told_apart_by: Two payments of the customer with the same PaidAt.
example_sql: SUM(p.Amount) OVER (ORDER BY p.PaidAt ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS RunningBalance
JOIN qe.Orders o ON o.OrderID = p.OrderID

traps.why: PaymentID in the window ORDER BY makes every row its own peer, which splits tied payments the same way a ROWS frame does.
traps.told_apart_by: Two payments of the customer with the same PaidAt.
example_sql: SUM(p.Amount) OVER (ORDER BY p.PaidAt, p.PaymentID) AS RunningBalance
JOIN qe.Orders o ON o.OrderID = p.OrderID

traps.why: A @From filter at the same query level as the window restarts the balance at @From and loses the opening balance.
traps.told_apart_by: A customer with a Settled payment before @From.
example_sql: SUM(p.Amount) OVER (ORDER BY p.PaidAt RANGE UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS RunningBalance
JOIN qe.Orders o ON o.OrderID = p.OrderID

min_improvement.basis: The triangular join visits about 16 billion rows for a 180k-payment partner. One ordered pass must be at least ten times faster on the partner case.
